data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Genuine reliability gain and mere checklist compliance are not separable within a single evaluation because they are the same phenomenon viewed from different temporal vantage points: compliance that tracks the right answer within the evaluation is genuine reliability within that evaluation, and the distinction only becomes meaningful prospectively when the evaluation distribution shifts; consequently, the search for a within-evaluation signature is a category error.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If one can construct within the evaluation a controlled distribution shift (e.g., held-out cases from a different sub-domain), the prospective question becomes partially testable within the evaluation and the category-error claim fails.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If error structure within the evaluation contains signatures of over-fitting to the checklist (e.g., errors exactly at rule boundaries), this is evidence of compliance rather than generalizable reasoning, and the distinction is partially detectable.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the evaluation includes process traces (justifications, reasoning protocols) that show whether participants recite rules versus reason independently, the distinction is detectable from process data even within a single evaluation.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the evaluation is large and diverse enough to serve as a proxy for the 'future distribution,' the within-evaluation performance already tests generalization and the category-error argument collapses.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Reliability is always defined relative to a distribution of cases. Within a single evaluation, the distribution is fixed. If the panel's checklist-compliant process produces the right answers on this distribution, it is reliable on this distribution by definition. The question 'is this genuine reliability or mere compliance?' presupposes a future distribution on which the two might diverge\u2014but that future distribution is absent from the single evaluation. Therefore no within-evaluation evidence can distinguish them, because the distinction is not a property of the single evaluation at all.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
